Question: Why did the British people turn on Winston Churchill after the war when he ran for prime minister?
Answer: I asked my father this same question about why Labour had been preferred to tthe Conservatives in 1945. My father had served in the RAF during the war - as a navigator - taking personnel and supplies into France to assist the Resistance. He said that he had voted Labour in the 1945 election. He cited four reasons for his vote: I think it is instructive to read the Conservative Party manifesto for the 1945 election. It is available at 1945 Conservative Party Manifesto. This document has every sign of being written by Winston Churchill. On demobilisation it says: “The broad and properly considered lines of the demobilisation proposals, based on age and length of service, which Mr. Bevin has elaborated with much wisdom, will be adhered to, and releases will be made as quickly as the condition of the tormented world permits.” By contrast the Labour Party manifesto (available at 1945 Labour Party Manifesto -) is silent on demobilisation. On Health the Conservative manifesto says: “The health services of the country will be made available to all citizens. Everyone will contribute to the cost, and no one will be denied the attention, the treatment or the appliances he requires because he cannot afford them. We propose to create a comprehensive health service covering the whole range of medical treatment from the general practitioner to the specialist, and from the hospital to convalescence and rehabilitation; and to introduce legislation for this purpose in the new Parliament.” On employment, the Conservative manifesto says: “In the White Paper presented to Parliament by the late administration are sound plans for avoiding the disastrous slumps and booms from which we used to suffer, but which all are united in being determined to avoid in the future. The Government accepts as one of its primary aims and responsibilities the maintenance of a high and stable level of employment.” On India the Conservative manifesto says: “The prowess of the Indian Army must not be overlooked in the framing of plans for granting India a fuller opportunity to achieve Dominion Status We should remember those friends who stood by us in our hour of peril, and should be ever mindful of our obligations towards minorities and the Indian States.” Looking back in hindsight, I think a Churchill government would actually have done a better job on all these items. I don’t think Churchill would have sent Mountbatten to India and I think he would have made a much greater effort to reconcile the parties and avoid the horrific bloodshed there. Clearly the substantive proposals put forward by the parties were not the reason for Labour’s victory in 1945. The Labour party quite simply did a much better job of putting their message across to the people - especially those in the armed services. Churchill had wanted to delay the election until after the defeat of Japan. He was distracted by the Potsdam conference and the strident demands of the Soviet Union. He took his re-election for granted and didn’t make the necessary effort required to achieve it. Churchill did win the election in 1951, which ushered in a long period of Conservative power. I think there were two major reasons for Conservative success in 1951: One of my earliest memories is walking around the neighbourhood of my grandmother’s home in South London. About every tenth house had been destroyed by bombs, and most of the lots still stayed there untouched with weeds growing over the ruins. Another memory is going to the shops with my aunt and seeing that she had to hand over ration tickets along with cash to buy basic foodstuffs.

Question: Since pre-industrial times, how has the atmospheric concentration of carbon dioxide changed?
Answer: In pre-industrial times there were no analytic techniques to accurately determine carbon dioxide levels. The best evidence comes from ice drill cores taken from Antarctica. When snow falls in Antarctica it traps air which becomes frozen in place as the snow consolidates into ice. The ice layers can be dated by several methods. Volcanic ash layers have distinctive chemical signatures. Thus the volcanic explosion of Mt Tambora in Indonesia in 1815 left distinctive ash layers around the world, including in the Antarctic ice cores. Similarly the eruption of Kuwae in Vanuatu in 1454 can be traced around the world. Analysis of the air trapped in the ice shows that pre industrial carbon dioxide levels were between 260 and 270 parts per million by volume, and that these levels were stable for the preceding 6000 years. There is a paper on pre industrial levels at The pre-industrial carbon dioxide level - Climatic Change and a paper on volcanic marker zones at http://www.researchgate.net/publication/251434348_A_2680_year_volcanic_record_from_the_DT401_East_Antarctic_ice_core/figures?lo=1 The most recent measured carbon dioxide levels are 417.3 parts per million from the Mauna Loa observatory in Hawaii and 415.4 parts per million from the Cape Grim observatory in Tasmania, Australia. Thus carbon dioxide levels have increased approximately 50% since pre industrial times. Climate deniers are fond of pointing out that human emissions of carbon dioxide are quite small compared to natural emissions. However the point is that prior to the industrial age, the carbon cycle was in balance, whereas now there is a small excess of emissions over absorptions. This excess amounts to about 2 parts per million per year. Thus over time, this small imbalance adds up to a very significant increase in overall concentrations of carbon dioxide.

Question: Is it possible to do geologic dating using uranium-lead methods on very old rocks? If so, how reliable are those dates?
Answer: The Uranium/Lead method of dating rocks relies on the fact that the uranium atom is unstable and over time decays into a series of unstable atoms, eventually ending up as a stable lead atom. By measuring how much of the uranium has decayed into lead it is possible to find the age of the rock. However, there is a problem. How can we decide whether the lead found in the sample was there already when the rock formed or was the result of uranium decay? The answer lies in a convenient fact about zircon crystals. When it crystalizes from molten rock, zircon (zirconium silicate ZrSiO4) will accept uranium atoms into its crystal structure but not lead atoms. Therefore, we can be sure that any lead found inside a zircon crystal came from the decay of uranium, and thus will give a reliable date. The key measure is the half life of uranium. This is the time taken for half the uranium in any sample to decay into lead. If for example there are equal numbers of uranium and lead atoms in the zircon, then it must have formed one half life of uranium ago. For this to work, the rock sample must have zircon crystals in it. There are a few other minerals with similar properties, but zircon is the most reliable. Fortunately, zircon is quite a common mineral. There is another wrinkle which adds reliability to the Uranium/Lead dating process. Uranium has two naturally occurring isotopes, and they decay into different lead isotopes at different rates. Uranium 235 decays into Lead 207 with a half life of 703.8 million years. Uranium 238 decays into Lead 206 with a half life of 4,468 million years. By measuring the concentrations of the four isotopes it is possible to get two independent estimates of the age of the crystals. If the two estimates agree, then they are said to be concordant and reliable. If they don’t agree than there may be some cause that has resulted in leakage of some isotopes. This may be due for example to a prolonged period of high temperatures Concordant results can give very reliable dates accurate to +/- 250,000 years. Reliable results are not possible with very young rocks – say less than 2 million years old. This is because the amount of lead in the crystals of these rocks would be very low and could be distorted by contamination. However, there is no problem with very old rocks. The age of the solar system is about 4.5 billion years - about the same as the half-life of Uranium 238. Therefore, in rocks the same age as the solar system, half of the original uranium 238 will still be present. Uranium 235 has a shorter half-life but 1.2% of the original uranium 235 will still be present and probably still detectable. Accurate results depend very much on meticulous sample collection and handling. Another factor that should be borne in mind is that the age determined is the age since the zircon crystalized. Zircon crystalizes at quite a high temperature. It is thus possible for solid zircon crystals to be carried in otherwise molten rock. The age determined will be older than the age for the bulk of the rock solidifying.

Aluminium makes up 8% of the rocky crust of the Earth by mass, but only 0.15% of the whole Earth. Iron makes up 32% by mass of the entire Earth, but only 5% of the crust. Magnesium is rarer in the crust than aluminium because although it is lithophile, for various reasons it stays in the mantle rather than the crust. For the Earth as a whole, magnesium is the second most abundant metal, making up 14% of the mass of the Earth. Sodium for some reason has about half the cosmic abundance of aluminium. The element with the highest boiling point is tungsten at 5,930 degrees Celsius. Tungsten has a high atomic number (74) and is very dense. In liquid form the tungsten atoms are more closely attracted to each other than similar high density metals like Osmium (AN 76).

Question: The earth’s core is iron, how pure is this? How do we know the composition?
Answer: There are several lines of evidence. First of all, the Earth’s mass and hence its density can be calculated from the orbital speed of satellites - like the Moon - around the Earth. The Earth’s density is 5.51 grams per cubic centimetre. This is higher than can be achieved through rocky materials, even when they are compressed by the immense pressures in the Earth’s interior. So there must be something denser in the centre of the Earth than the common rocky materials found in the exterior. The study of meteorites gives clues to what this material could be. Meteorites are thought to be the leftover materials from the formation of planets in the inner solar system. Some are fragments of failed planets that disintegrated due to collisions. Some meteorites appear to be pure leftover material that never formed a protoplanet while others appear to be fragments of these protoplanets. These fragments are of two main types - stony (rocky), and nickel iron. There are also some mixed stony/iron meteorites. It seems a good bet that the outer layers of the Earth are represented by the stony meteorites and the inner layers by the nickel/irons. Next the study of seismic waves gives clues to the structure of the Earth. The exact pattern of seismic waves around the globe suggests that the Earth has a solid inner core and an outer liquid core. Next the study of the cosmic abundance of elements suggests that iron (element 26) is relatively enriched. This is because iron is the last in the sequence of element synthesis that generates energy. When a massive star has accumulated iron in its interior, it has nowhere further to go. It’s explosion in a supernova spreads heavy elements including iron across the cosmos. Many responders on Quora claim that the components of the early Earth differentiated on the basis of density. This is actually incorrect and those responders should know better. It is true that the rocky and iron components of the Earth separated. This is due to the fact that liquid silicates and liquid iron are like oil and water - they don’t mix. It is also true that the liquid iron component of the Earth settled into the core, because it is denser than the liquid rocky silicates. However the final destination of other elements depended on their chemical affinities - not their densities. Precious metals - like gold and platinum - did mainly end up in the core because they are siderophile (“iron loving”) elements. However other dense elements like the radioactive elements uranium, thorium and potassium 40 ended up in the mantle because they are lithophile (“rock loving”) elements. Unlike the claims of these ignorant responders, there are little or no radioactive elements in the core of the Earth. It is difficult on the surface of the Earth to replicate the extreme temperatures and pressures that exist in the core. However many recent papers suggest that under the extreme pressure, pure iron is crystallizing in the centre of the Earth. One such paper is at New theory explains how Earth's inner core remains solid despite extreme heat The latent heat released by the crystallization of the solid core likely makes the boundary between the solid and the liquid core the hottest place within the Earth - at 6,000 degrees C rivalling the surface of the sun. So far, in the 4.5 billion year history of the Earth, only about 25% of the nickel/iron core has solidified. Because of the latest heat released by solidification and the heat from the decay of radioactive elements in the mantle, It will be at least another 8 billion years before the core completely solidifies. By then the Earth will have been engulphed by the expanding red giant phase of the sun.

Question: What is bord and pillar mining?
Answer: Bord and Pillar is also called Room and Pillar mining. It’s a mining method applicable to more or less flat lying deposits like coal or salt. Parallel “entries” (tunnels) are driven into the deposit. At regular intervals crosscuts are driven leaving a pattern of rectangular pillars which support the roof. The exact size and configuration of the entries depends on the depth of the deposit and the strength characteristics of the roof. Sometimes the pillars will be left in place indefinitely to support the roof. Sometimes the pillars will be “robbed” on retreat and the roof left to subside.

Question: Why is earth's core so hot? Could earth exist with a solid core?
Answer: The Earth does have a solid core. This is known from a study of seismic waves. There several kinds of seismic waves, but the most important are P waves and S waves. P waves can pass through both solids and liquids, but S waves can only go through solids. By timing the arrival of waves from earthquakes at seismic stations around the globe, geophysicists have built up a model of the Earth. At the centre of the Earth is a solid core. The exact composition of this core is disputed, but many scientists believe it to be almost pure crystallised iron. A nature article explains the evidence for this at A more popular version of this article, not protected by a paywall is available at New theory explains how Earth's inner core remains solid despite extreme heat. The outer core is a liquid mixture of iron, nickel and other elements. The boundary between the solid inner core and the liquid outer core is called the Bullen Discontinuity. This discontinuity is believed to be the hottest part of the Earth, because of latent heat released by the solidifying iron. The temperature here is believed to be about 6,000 degrees Celsius - about the same as the surface of the sun. The reason that the iron can solidify despite the high temperature is due to the extreme pressure. The differentiation of the Earth into the metallic core and the rocky outer layer of the mantle happened early in the life of the Earth when the whole planet was molten. The differentiation occurred because liquid iron and liquid silicates are like oil and water - they don’t mix. Some elements preferred to go with iron. They are called siderophile (“iron loving”) elements, and include gold and platinum, as well as nickel and cobalt. The major radioactive elements, uranium, thorium and potassium 40 prefer silicates - they are among the lithophile (“rock loving”) elements. Thus, contrary to what some other responders claim, there are no significant radioactive elements in the core, and the core is not heated by radioactive decay. The mantle contains most of the radioactive elements and is heated by their decay. This heating slows the escape of heat from the core. Geological processes at the mantle crust boundary have enriched the crust in radioactive minerals, creating significant ore resources, but the mantle is so much larger than the crust that most of the radioactivity remains in the mantle. It is estimated that it will 9 billion years for the liquid core to completely solidify. By then the Earth will have been engulfed in the Sun’s red giant stage.

Question: What is the most common element on Earth (not counting hydrogen)? Why is it so common compared to other elements? What makes it special from others that make it more abundant than others?

In the crust of the Earth, oxygen atoms make up more than 60% of the content. By mass, oxygen is also the most common element making up 32% of the mass of the Earth. The triple alpha process is initiated when two helium 4 nuclei (alpha particles) combine to form a beryllium 8 nucleus. This happens in the core of our sun. But beryllium 8 is exceedingly unstable and in our sun the beryllium 8 rapidly decays back to helium. However when the temperature and pressure is about ten times more intense, it can happen that a third helium 4 nucleus combines with the beryllium 8 to form carbon 12, which is stable. And then a fourth helium nucleus can combine with the carbon 12 to form oxygen 16 - also stable. Thus carbon and oxygen build up in these stars. The stars may later explode, spreading carbon and oxygen and other atoms across space. It is thought that there was a supernova explosion close to where our own solar system was forming 4.6 billion years ago. As the sun coalesced out of the earlier gas cloud, the central portions of the solar system heated up. Volatile components that were not part of the sun were expelled from the inner solar system. Gasses like hydrogen, helium, hydrocarbons and carbon dioxide were pushed out to the outer solar system. Oxygen survived because it had combined with silicon to form rocky dust particles, with a high melting temperature. Iron and nickel survived too. Thus the material left in the inner solar system, which eventually formed the four inner planets was primarily silicon and oxygen - in the form of silica or silicates.

Question: Were CO2 levels substantially higher nearly 650,000 years ago (climate change, earth science)?
Answer: The best data for past levels of gas in the atmosphere come from ice cores from Antarctica. When snow falls, it traps air. When the snow compacts those air bubbles are sealed in. The ice cores from Dome C give the following record for greenhouse gasses. Prior to human industrialization the highest level found in the cores was just under 300 parts per million. That was 330,000 years ago. There are two obvious questions about this data. First how carefully were the samples taken and are they reliable. The site says: “Methods At the Bern laboratory, four to six samples of approximately 8 grams from each depth level (0.55m intervals) in the ice core are crushed under vacuum conditions. The sample container is connected to a cold trap for several minutes to release air from the clathrates and the air is then expanded to a measuring cell where a laser measures absorption in a vibration–rotation transition line of the CO2 molecule. Calibration is done using a CO2 -in-air standard gas of 251.65 parts per million by volume (ppmv) scaled on the WMO mole fraction scale. At Grenoble (Laboratory of Glaciology, Geophysics and Environment) one to three ice samples of about 40 grams each are crushed under vacuum conditions, and after about 20 minutes the extracted gas is expanded in the sample loop of a gas chromatograph and analyzed. Depending on the amount of extracted air, three to five successive analyses are done. To avoid possible effects of water-vapor interference, the CO2 ratio is calculated as the ratio of the CO2 peak to the air (O2 + N2) peak. Calibration is done using an Air Liquide standard scaled on CSIRO standards (172.8 ppmv, 260.3 ppmv, and 321.1 ppmv). Uncertainty is a few ppmv; measurement error for the Bern laboratory is given in the data file, and the Grenoble Lab generally compares within a few ppmv for the common time interval.” The second question is how reliable are the dates. There are several methods used in dating. Major volcanic eruptions spread dust worldwide. Each eruption has its own unique chemical signature. Thus the ice cores can be correlated with marine sediments and other sources to arrive at a consistent date. Another dating method uses beryllium 10 isotopes. Beryllium 10 is constantly created in the atmosphere by cosmic rays. Once locked into the ice, the beryllium 10 decays to boron 10 with a half life of 1.36 million years. By measuring the beryllium and boron isotopes, an age since burial can be calculated. Ice Dome C has the longest record but there are other sites in Antarctica which have yielded ice cores.

Even with concordant results, there are still some issues to be considered. The age calculated is from the time the zircon crystallized. This may well be earlier than the time at which the rock as a whole solidified. If the rock is sedimentary, then the zircon crystals may be much older than when the sedimentary rock was deposited. Question: How accurate is carbon dating, and what use can you make with it?
Answer: Carbon dating in theory can be highly accurate, but it needs meticulous attention to detail and a deep understanding of the process to achieve accuracy. Carbon dating relies on measuring the ratio of carbon 14 to carbon 12 in a sample. Carbon has two stable isotopes - carbon 12 and carbon 13. Carbon 14 is an unstable isotope with a half life of 5,730 years. On Earth 99% of carbon is Carbon 12, 1% is Carbon 13 and 1.5 atoms in a quadrillion are Carbon 14. Cosmic rays striking the atmosphere produce neutrons. The neutrons react with Nitrogen 14 to produce carbon 14 plus a proton according to the formula: The carbon 14 oxidises to carbon dioxide. Plants absorb carbon dioxide and through photosynthesis convert it to solid plant material. The carbon 14 is absorbed along with the carbon 12 and carbon 13. While the plant is alive, the ratio of carbon 14 to carbon 12 is the same as in the atmosphere. After the plant dies, the carbon 14 decays back to nitrogen 14. After 5,730 years, half of the carbon 14 has gone. By measuring the ratio of carbon 14 to carbon 12 and carbon 13, it is possible to calculate the time that has elapsed since the plant material was created. Assumptions that are made to arrive at a result are: It is known that the ratio of carbon 14 has not been constant. It varies with cosmic ray intensity. By comparing with other dating methods - such as tree rings, it has been possible to develop a correction for varying carbon 14 concentrations - as in the graph below Thus if the the uncorrected age is calculated to be 30,000 years, the real age is 34,000 years. Mass spectrometers are amazingly sensitive and accurate devices. Their accuracy must be maintained by regular use of standard samples of known age. Sample preparation is complex and must be done meticulously. Contamination with modern carbon is a very real issue with older samples. A 38,000 year old sample contains only 1% of the original carbon 14. A small amount of modern carbon contamination will give a large error. Contamination can occur at any stage of the process from collection to sample preparation. Things like microbial growth on the sample or inclusion of modern air must be guarded against. Any dates older than 40,000 years must be considered suspect. Dates younger than this determined by reputable laboratories can be considered highly accurate. It must be remembered that the date determined is the date on which the plant material was formed. Thus in New Mexico we used carbon dating to determine the age of wood used in habitations. But, in the New Mexico desert, wood can survive undecomposed for hundreds of years. The date determined is the date of the wood. It could have been used to build a hut many years later. Also in a tree the center of the tree will have an older date than the outside. Other organic material can also used - for example animal remains. The date will reflect the age of the food eaten. Shells cannot be used. This is because the calcium carbonate in shells likely was dissolved in water and did not represent the carbon 14 in the atmosphere at the time the shell was formed. In summary, carbon dating can be used to determine the date of organic material up to about 40,000 years old. The organic material could for example be wooden artefacts. If determined by a reputable laboratory after careful sample collection and treatment, the dates are very accurate.

Question: Why do metals and minerals show up in some parts of the Earth and not in others?
Answer: Ore formation is a whole subject of its own. The text book Ore Geology and Industrial Minerals: An Introduction by Anthony Evans is a good start. It’s 400 pages long, but its designed for first year students - so in many ways it just skims the surface. Here is one of the many diagrams from the book: The concentration of different elements into different zones of the Earth started when the Earth was still molten. The Earth’s composition was mostly iron and silicates (silicon and oxygen combined with various metals. Silicates and iron are like oil and water - they don’t mix. Certain elements - like nickel, cobalt and gold preferred to go with the iron and ended up mostly in the core of the Earth. Other elements preferred to go with the silicates. As well as light metals like aluminium, the rock loving metals included some dense ones like uranium and thorium. The Earth started out hot. Adding the original heat was heat from decaying radioactive elements - like the uranium and thorium and potassium 40. The rocky mantle of the Earth became semi solid, but still partly plastic and subject to upwelling convection currents. The convection currents caused interaction with the solidifying crust of the Earth. This interaction caused certain elements to be enriched in the crust, and others diluted. As large masses of molten rock cooled, various compounds within the rocks began to crystalize. Since some compounds crystalize at higher temperatures than others, certain elements like chromium and platinum settled into enriched layers. The Bushveld Igneous Complex in South Africa is an example. While the rocks were cooling water and other liquids circulated through the solidifying rocks. Sometimes certain elements, including gold would dissolve in the circulating fluids and then precipitate out when the temperature or chemical environment changed. The evolution of photosynthesising plants in the oceans caused a huge change about 2.4 billion years ago. The oceans changed from being reducing to oxidising. As a result soluble ferrous ions were turned into insoluble ferric ions and precipitated out to form the huge iron ore beds of Western Australia, Brazil and Michigan. Oxidation also affected the solubility of other elements. Erosion wore away the rocks, reducing them to individual grains. The action of water in rivers and wave action in the sea separated the grains by density, or sometimes by chemical resistance, forming immense placer deposits. As noted - this is just a summary. Talented geologists who can use science to discover valuable deposits are much in demand.

Question: Given how old the Earth is, is it possible that all dry land was at one point underwater? What evidence is there for such?
Answer: The volume of water in the oceans (1.335 billion cubic kilometres) is enough to cover the entire surface of the Earth (510 million square kilometres) to a depth of 2,600 metres (8,600 feet). So its possible that Earth was once completely covered in water. However the evidence is against it. The crust of the Earth falls into two basic categories - the continents and the ocean floors. The continents are made of lighter granitic rocks. The ocean floors are made of denser basaltic rocks. Because they are lighter the continents “float” above the oceanic crust, by about 3,500 metres. The segregation into continental and oceanic crust has continued since the Earth was formed and is still happening. Thus there was less continental crust during the early stages of Earth’s history - which might suggest the possibility of a planet wide ocean. However plate tectonics and volcanic activity are driven by the internal heat of the Earth. In earlier times the heat was greater, partly because some of it came from the formation of the Earth and has now escaped and partly because some comes from radioactive decay, which is gradually decreasing as the radioactive elements decay. For example Uranium 235 still contributes to internal heat, but its half life is only 710 million years, so only 2% of Earth’s original Uranium 235 still exists. Hence in the early Earth it is likely that plate tectonics and volcanism were much more active and energetic which would have created a bigger difference in elevations and kept areas above water. The stable centres of the continents are known to geologists as cratons. Cratons are by and large old, and flat, high lying areas, which contain mostly igneous and metamorphic rocks. They have very limited amounts of sedimentary rocks formed under water. This suggests that most cratons have been dry land for at least the last 3 billion years. Some geologists support the Snowball Earth Hypothesis (http://astronomy.com/news/2019/04/the-story-of-snowball-earth) . This supposes that the entire Earth was frozen 650 million years ago, and so covered in solid water. However, even then some areas would likely have been exposed. So in summary, its not likely that the Earth was completely covered in water in the past. However it is much more likely that it will be completely covered in the future. Eventually the internal heat of the Earth will drop to the point where plate tectonics and volcanism cease. At that point there will be nothing pushing up mountains. Erosion will gradually wear away the high ground and Earth will become a water world. However this won’t happen in our life times.

Question: What kind of rock is taconite?
Answer: Taconite is a very hard banded iron rock. It was formed during the Great Oxygenation Event (GOE) when blue green algae in the world’s oceans started producing oxygen in large quantities, 2.5 billion years ago. The oxygen converted ferrous (Fe++) ions dissolved in the oceans to insoluble ferric (Fe++) ions. The iron was precipitated onto the ocean floor. Periodic changes in the chemical environment led to deposition of bands of iron rich and iron poor sediment. Taconite is mined on a very large scale around Lake Superior. Taconite ore typically contains 25 to 30% iron. It is upgraded by grinding to a fine powder and then using a magnetic separator to recover the magnetite (iron oxide) particles. These are then mixed with a binder and fired to make pellets. The pellets typically contain 65% iron and are also referred to as “taconite”. Taconite provides most of the iron ore used in the US steel industry.

Question: Is the Earth's core solid, liquid, or something else?
Answer: The Earth’s outer core is known to be liquid and the inner core is solid. This structure is projected after detailed technical study of the behaviour of seismic waves passing through the Earth. When the Earth was young, it was completely liquid, due to the heat generated by its formation. Just four elements constituted more than 90% of the mass of the Earth. These four elements were oxygen, silicon iron and magnesium. The oxygen silicon and magnesium combined to form rocky silicates. The iron remained separate. Liquid iron and liquid silicates are like oil and water - they don’t mix. Some of the minor constituents like nickel, cobalt, gold, platinum, and other siderophile (”iron-loving”) elements were chemically attracted to the iron. Many other elements, like sodium, potassium, uranium and thorium were attracted to the silicates. Because it is denser than silicates, the iron, with its associated siderophile elements settled into the core of the planet. Over billions of years the Earth has cooled. The cooling is partly offset by heat from the decay of radioactive elements in the mantle. Under the intense pressure at the centre of the Earth, and the cooling, the iron in the central core began to solidify. It is very difficult to replicate conditions in the core of the Earth, but it is believed that the iron is forming into nearly pure iron crystals, leaving the remaining liquid core enriched in the siderophile elements. The crystallisation is apparently not symmetrical. A report at Earth's Crystallized Iron Inner Core Could Be Lopsided, Study Suggests says that seismic waves travelling from pole to pole travel 3% faster than waves from the equator. The authors say this is due to the solid core not being perfectly spherical, but lopsided.

Question: Does the Cambrian explosion provide evidence for intelligent design?
Answer: “Evidence” is too strong a word - but the amazing diversification of life at the beginning of the Cambrian is at least suggestive of the possibility of intelligent design. The concept is hotly denied by nearly all biologists, but their arguments have a few holes in them. A large number (perhaps 85%) of the phyla recognised by biologists came into existence at the beginning of the Cambrian period. For most of the Earth’s history, encompassing billions of years, the only evidence of life is of microbial life, most famously the stromatolite microbial mats dating back 4 billion years. Then, just before the Cambrian, there are two sets of fossilised evidence of multicellular organisms. These are the Ediacaran fauna and the small shelly fauna. The Ediacaran fauna have been found at several sites around the world, in the form of impressions in fine grained rock. They had no bony structures, and they appear to have gone extinct and left no descendants. The small shelly fauna left small shells, which may have been part of larger creatures. Then immediately after this, in the early Cambrian, we have a sudden proliferations of all kinds of new fossils. It certainly appears in the fossil record like an “explosion”. Even Charles Darwin was aware of this issue. He said “To the question of why we do not find rich fossiliferous deposits belonging to these…periods prior to the Cambrian system, I can give no satisfactory answer”. To explain this Cambrian explosion it is said that wasn’t really an explosion, but more of a slow fuse as it lasted 20 million years. However most of the new phyla came into existence in the early Cambrian - perhaps over 5 million years or less. It is said that molecular evidence from modern phyla suggests that they diverged well before the Cambrian explosion. However if this is the case, why didn’t they leave fossil remains? It is said that they didn’t leave fossils because they hadn’t developed hard body parts. But the Ediacaran fauna didn’t have hard body parts either, and they left fossils. It is said that chemical conditions weren’t right to preserve calcareous parts - but the small shellies left preserved parts. I think that it’s possible that there was intervention which speeded up evolution. This was no supernatural intervention by a divine omniscient being. Rather it was the work of tinkerers. The failed experiments of the Ediacaran and small shelly faunas show that that could have been their initial work. Intervention would have made changes to genes in different phyla, which molecular scientists now interpret as earlier diversification. The incorporation of prokaryotes into the eukaryote cells as organelles like the mitochondria also suggests tinkering. In case you think this theory is far fetched, it has been suggested by sober scientists that humans might one day do the same thing. An article in the usually staid journal Astrophysics and Space Science (Developing ecospheres on transiently habitable planets: the genesis project) suggests that humans may one day attempt to speed up evolution on promising exoplanets. If serious scientists suggest such a course of action, why couldn’t it have happened on Earth? It seems to me that opposition to the idea any kind of intelligent input to species diversification in the Cambrian explosion is more ideological based than evidence based.

The heat derives partly from original heat of formation and partly from the decay of radioactive material in the mantle. Both sources of heat are getting less. It is estimated that plate tectonics will cease in about 1.4 billion years. After that, there will be nothing to offset erosion. There are three possible outcomes for Planet Earth. Waterworld - the land and mountains all erode down into the oceans. The average depth will be about 2,700 metres. Snowball World - because carbon dioxide is no longer recycled, global warming falls away and the average temperature falls below zero degrees. The oceans freeze. Desert World - the increasing radiation from the sun as it evolves, and less protection as Earth’s magnetic field weakens as a result of the cooling core, increase evaporation of the oceans. The powerful greenhouse effect of water vapour causes a further increase in evaporation. The radiation splits the water molecules and hydrogen is lost to space. Eventually all the oceans are gone and Earth resembles current day Venus.

Since the chalk accumulated at a rate of one foot every 200 to 1,000 years and the rows are often about four feet apart, there must have been 800 to four thousand years between rows. The Scientific American article at http://www.scientificamerican.com/article/chalk-flints-and-the-age-of-the-ear/struggles with the answer. A response by Amanda Lane at The Geological Society of London - Flint Formed in Chalk. has a beetter explanation. Her theory is based on the fact chalk is an alkaline rock. Before the silica can be deposited the chalk grains must be dissolved by acid. Bacterial activity in the sediment within the seabed generated hydrogen sulphide which, when migrating towards the seabed/seawater interface, met dissolved oxygen migrating down in the sediment. Where the dissolved oxygen and hydrogen sulphide met, acidic conditions were generated, carbonate was dissolved and silica precipitated to form flint. The silica that formed the flint derived from silica fixed in the skeletal structure of many marine organisms. Every now and then conditions changed and a new level developed where the hydrogen sulfide met the acid. Other theories including animal burrows and Milankovitch cycles are discussed at 49 – The Problem with Chalk and Flint

Name: Chris Seymour
Question: What is the purpose of the greenhouse effect on Earth?
Answer: The term greenhouse effect is a bit of a misnomer, because as Paul Noel points out in his answer to a related question, it doesn’t really work in the same way as a greenhouse. However it is a very real effect and it keeps the Earth warmer than it otherwise would be. Carbon dioxide and some other gasses in the atmosphere are transparent to visible light but partially opaque to infra red wavelengths. Much of the energy from the sun arrives by visible light. But energy emitted by the Earth is mostly at infra red wavelengths. Much of the energy emitted by the Earth’s surface is thus absorbed by the atmosphere and half is re-emitted back to the ground. In this way the Earth is warmer than it otherwise would be. Without the greenhouse effect, the Earth’s surface would be about 32 degrees C colder than at present. The oceans would be frozen and life would be very much restricted. Moreover not only does the greenhouse effect provide a suitable habitat for life on the present Earth, it has also provided a mechanism that has kept the Earth at a suitable temperature for life during its entire existence. As the sun has evolved, it has steadily become more active. In the early solar system, the sun emitted only about 70% of its current energy output. On Earth this effect of the faint early sun was offset because carbon dioxide was much, much more common in the atmosphere. Life, through plant photosynthesis, has gradually reduced the concentration of carbon dioxide - acting in effect like a giant thermostat to keep the planet’s temperature at a level suitable for life over billions of years. If the Earth was created by God, then He was a brilliant designer to have come up with this solution. He may have had other purposes for the Greenhouse Effect, but this was certainly one of them. And the Greenhouse Effect is quite a powerful argument for the existence of a God designer. If, as I believe, God was not involved, then there has been a truly fortuitous circumstance that has kept the Earth at a temperature suitable for life over billions of years.
